title: Rh Blood Group System: D Antigen and Rh Immune Globulin
summary: RhD typing, weak D, Du interpretation and prevention of Rh hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn.
objectives: Explain the significance of the D antigen in transfusion and pregnancy.
Interpret weak D typing results in donors vs recipients.
State the indications for Rh immune globulin prophylaxis.

highYield: Anti-D is the most clinically significant Rh antibody and is immune (IgG), not naturally occurring.
Weak D recipients are treated as Rh-negative to avoid immunization; weak D donors are treated as Rh-positive.
RhIg prevents anti-D formation in Rh-negative mothers carrying an Rh-positive fetus.

rows: RhIg at 28 weeks and postpartum if baby is D-pos

quickReview.mnemonic: Weak D? Recipient gets negative, donor counts positive.

deepStudy.introduction: The Rh system contains many antigens; D is the most immunogenic. Anti-D can cause hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn (HDFN) and hemolytic transfusion reactions.

sections.heading: Weak D and partial D
sections.body: Weak D (formerly Du) shows negative or weak reactions at immediate spin but positive at AHG with adsorption/elution. Partial D individuals can form anti-D because they lack part of the D epitope — treat clinically as Rh-negative when receiving blood.

sections.heading: HDFN prevention
sections.body: RhIg (anti-D immunoglobulin) is given to Rh-negative, D-unsensitized mothers at 28 weeks of gestation, within 72 hours of delivery of an Rh-positive infant, and after any fetomaternal hemorrhage event (e.g., miscarriage, amniocentesis, trauma).

deepStudy.clinicalSignificance: Anti-D crosses the placenta (IgG) and can cause severe fetal anemia and hydrops fetalis. Prevention with RhIg is one of the great successes of transfusion medicine.
deepStudy.labInterpretation: A negative D typing in a patient with anti-D in the serum suggests partial D or a mixed-field reaction — investigate before issuing blood.
examTraps: Weak D testing is NOT required on recently transfused patients — mixed-field reactions can mislead.
Do not give Rh-positive platelets to a childbearing-potential Rh-negative patient without RhIg cover.

memoryHooks.text: D = Dangerous during pregnancy (anti-D is IgG, crosses placenta).
memoryHooks.funny: Bantay says: 'Anti-D is the ex na ayaw mag-move on — laging nagbabalik at umaatake.'
